name: Untimely Malfunction
notes: The ability names only the "Choose one" line: each bullet belongs to that line (faceLines drops bullets) and a modal ability may name at most one line per substantive mode. The third mode is the closest the target vocabulary reaches for "one or two target creatures": TargetSpec has a count but no minimum, so { count: 2, optional: true } is "up to two" - it also allows zero targets, where the card requires at least one.

issues: • One or two target creatures can't block this turn. — expected a mode that requires at least one and at most two targets; with no creature on the battlefield this mode cannot legally be chosen (CR 601.2c: the announced targets must meet the required minimum; 700.2 modal choice must be legal) — scripted { op: 'cant-block', target: { kind: 'creature', count: 2, optional: true }, duration: 'eot' } — `optional: true` is the vocabulary's "up to" (src/cards/types.ts:39 `optional?: boolean // "up to one"`, legal.ts:180 renders it as "up to two target creatures"), and legal.ts:213/361 let a cast through when an optional spec has zero options, so the mode is castable with zero targets and does nothing. The script's own `notes` admits this ("TargetSpec has a count but no minimum … it also allows zero targets, where the card requires at least one"). The blind scenarios only exercise one and two targets, so they pass without catching it. — CR 601.2c / 700.2

Choose one — (whole card, covers accounting) — expected every printed line claimed — scripted the single ability's `text` is only "Choose one —" and there is no `covers` field; `npm run scripts:render` scores that one line 1.00 and never scores the three bullets, so no rendered check exists for the mode bodies. Not a rules error under the faceLines convention (bullets are dropped), but it means the bullet wording is unverified by the round-trip score. Modes 1 (destroy target artifact) and 2 (change-targets / 'single-target-spell-or-ability' / how 'change-one', which the engine implements as a forced move to another legal target per CR 115.7) are otherwise correct, and `duration: 'eot'` correctly matches "this turn" (cleared via eotFlags at cleanup). — CR 115.7

• One or two target creatures can't block this turn. — expected A required minimum of one target and a maximum of two ('one or two target creatures'): the mode is an illegal mode choice when no creature can be targeted, and the spell can never be cast with zero creatures named (CR 601.2c, 700.2d). — scripted { op: 'cant-block', target: { kind: 'creature', count: 2, optional: true }, duration: 'eot' } — TargetSpec.optional is documented in src/cards/types.ts:39 as 'up to one'/'up to N', and src/engine/legal.ts:213/261/361 exempts optional requirements from the 'no legal options' gate, so mode 3 is castable with ZERO targets and remains a legal mode with an empty board. The script's own notes admit this ('it also allows zero targets, where the card requires at least one'). — CR 601.2c, 700.2d, 115.3

Choose one — (whole modal ability) — expected The ability's text should carry the modal line and its three bullets so the render round-trip actually re-derives the printed modes. — scripted ability.text is only 'Choose one —'. `npm run scripts:render` therefore reports card score 1.00 against a two-word string; none of the three mode bodies (destroy artifact / change target / can't block) is exercised by the round-trip at all, so the 1.00 score is not evidence that the modes are covered. Secondary/process issue, not itself a rules error. — CR 700.2

• Change the target of target spell or ability with a single target. — expected Target must be changed to a different legal target if one exists; if none exists the target is unchanged. — scripted change-targets / how:'change-one' on kind 'single-target-spell-or-ability' — src/engine/ops/copy-clone.ts:288-292 offers only `others` for change-one and falls back to keeping the target when the list is empty. This clause is CORRECT; recorded only to show it was checked. — CR 115.7, 115.7b
